description: Apple rose ~6.2% on 2025-05-12 in a market-wide rally after the U.S. and China announced a 90-day tariff truce (S&P 500 +3.3%, Nasdaq +4.4%). Apple did file an 8-K that same day - but it is a routine debt offering (Item 8.01, with underwriting agreement, indenture, and legal opinion exhibits) that has nothing to do with the move. This is the HARD honesty case: unlike coin_2026-06-05, retrieval here returns real, recent, same-day company documents, and the system must still decline to explain the move with them.

event.note: The U.S. and China agreed to temporarily cut tariffs (U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods to 30%, Chinese tariffs on U.S. imports to 10%). Megacap tech rallied broadly: Tesla ~+7%, Apple ~+6%, Nvidia ~+5%. The cause is macro and sector-wide, not company-specific.

trigger.verified_fact: Close-to-close gain of ~6.2% on 2025-05-12, from $198.53 to $210.79.
trigger.note: Real daily closes from Yahoo Finance. Also the first UP move in the fixture set.

filing.note: This filing IS indexed and IS retrievable - that is the entire point. It is a debt issuance, not a disclosure capable of moving the equity 6%.

ground_truth.one_line: A macro tariff-truce rally lifted the whole market and megacap tech; Apple's same-day 8-K is an unrelated notes offering. Correct behavior is 'no clear catalyst found'.
ground_truth.key_facts_note: Empty by design. The filing is real but irrelevant, so there are no filing-grounded facts that explain the move. Correctness is not scored for this fixture.
market_context: The U.S. and China announced a 90-day tariff truce on 2025-05-12.
S&P 500 +3.26%, Nasdaq +4.35%, Dow +1,160 points that session.
Apple manufactures the large majority of iPhones in China, so it is especially tariff-sensitive.
ground_truth.market_context_note: Explains the move, but none of it is in any SEC filing. A system limited to filings cannot and should not assert it.
ground_truth.expected_citation: none - no company filing explains this move
ground_truth.naive_failure_mode: The dangerous failure is grabbing the same-day notes-offering 8-K and spinning it into a reason ('Apple raised capital, signaling confidence'). A debt issuance is routine treasury activity and does not move a megacap 6%. Retrieval WILL return this document; the system must judge it insufficient rather than treat proximity and recency as relevance.

provenance.sources: Filing identity and exhibit types read from EDGAR accession 0001140361-25-018400; tariff-truce market reaction from contemporaneous financial press (CNBC, Yahoo Finance); daily closes from Yahoo Finance.
